pr_title: Add default board to new projects, remove uncategorized pseudo-board
pr_body:
On creation of an empty project (no template) a default board will be created instead of falling back to the uneditable pseudo-board.

Every project now has to have exactly one default boards. As a consequence, you cannot unset a board as default, instead you have to set another board as default. Existing projects will be modified using a cron job, additionally this check will run every midnight by default.

Deleting the default board is not allowed, you have to set another board as default to do it.

Fixes #29873
Fixes #14679 along the way
Fixes #29853

Co-authored-by: delvh <dev.lh@web.de>

It seems that there is a hard requirement for "there must be one default board" ?

Could it relax the requirement and make the code more robust. For example, do not force users to set one default board, but only "select" a default board: use the one with `default=true` if exist, otherwise use the oldest board? If no board, then create a new one.

@wxiaoguang
@lunny

Currently, the default "Uncategorized" board that you see when opening a project without a default board doesn't actually exist in DB, it is generated dynamically on render when opening a project which doesn't have a default board. Every issue not assigned to another board is automatically on "Uncategorized".

What this PR does is replace it with a default "Backlog" board for every project instead. This new board does exist in the DB, so it can be treated as every other board and e. g. be renamed, change colour and be deleted if you set any other board as default. Every issue that previously appeared on "Uncategorized" will now appear on "Backlog" -> for the users, the only noticeable changes will be the rename and the ability to rename the board, nothing else will change with the behaviour.

Two "Backlog" columns? It can be renamed then, you can also have two "Uncategorized" columns currently.

Use the oldest board as default if no default is set? I don't think it's something I would expect as a user. What is the problem with forcing a default board per project? It isn't impacting the user's options in any way. By enforcing it, we ensure that new issues appear where they are expected to instead of a random board which was never ever set as default.

> @wxiaoguang What would you like to be tested? The migration, the automatic creation of a default column....?

Exactly, there is a cronjob to ensure that if one happens somehow, it will be fixed automatically.

Honestly I'm tired of rewriting the behaviour over and over again.

Why is a migration still necessary? The cron job runs on start and also adds a default "Uncategorized" board to projects without one, that's exactly what was done in the migration before.

Why is a cronjob wrong? I don't expect a `getDefaultBoard` method to create or modify columns...

Who am I supposed to listen to, @delvh who asked for a cronjob or @wxiaoguang who is against one or @lunny who requests a migration? Don't take it personal, I just don't understand at this point what I am supposed to do to get this PR done which started with 10 LOC 🥲

We can create a migration and also provide a doctor command but not the cron job. I cannot imagine we will have more and more cron jobs to check the inconsistent problems in the background if we do that.

> We can create a migration and also provide a doctor command but not the cron job.

The "doctor" system is also a disaster, unless it is really really necessary, I would suggest do not touch it too much. It is very difficult for end users to use, and not friendly in docker, not well tested and have many bugs (update: and it is very unfriendly, end users have to open an issue here ask "why 500" then be told to run "doctor", that's really unfriendly)

That's why I suggest to make the system self-healing from beginning, just keep things simple. IMO a correct migration + self-healing + test-code is good enough.

----

Disclaimer: that's just my opinion. Please TOC decide.

I thought we could achieve this through a cronjob.
Also my bad, I was under the impression initially that the `doctor fix` commands were periodically executed in a cronjob which apparently isn't the case.

Neither doctor nor cronjob are good solutions and I agree we should reduce those. A good place to fix would be a one-time action during startup, e.g. migration, or one-time action when a project is opened.

@lunny @wxiaoguang @delvh

1. Readded migration which adds the default column to projects without one and unsets columns as default if multiple are set
2. Added the same check to the getDefaultBoard method to run on every project view -> the error that there is no default column cannot appear any longer (is that the thing you called "self-healing"?)

issue_context.title: Allow editing default project column
issue_context.body:
### Feature Description

When creating an org project, and adding a second column, only the second column can be edited, the default column can't.

Instead, all columns should be able to change their settings (however, for the default board only `name` and `color`, not `delete` or `unpin` to avoid inconsistent states).

Extract from #23318

_No response_

Sorry but this migration seems broken ....

If the "SELECT" results are stable and never change, this `for` loop is right.

BUT, by each `SELECT` and for-loop, the "project boards" are changed. The next `SELECT`, it should still process the first page results, but not skip `start`.


For example: 150 projects.

1. First loop: `SELECT` gets 1-50 projects and updates them.
2. Second loop: `SELECT` gets "the second page" from "51-150", then it gets 101-150 projects.
